payload.comment:
Reporting stage is internally consistent and complete. All deterministic cross-checks pass: (1) abstain_rate × 7180 = 2711 matches human_review_count exactly; (2) test_coverage + abstain_rate = 1.0; (3) confusion matrix row sums equal per-class supports and total 7180; (4) macro_recall, macro_precision, macro_f1, and accuracy all reproduce from the confusion matrix; (5) selective_risk and threshold correspond to the 0.8 target_validation_coverage row in the risk_coverage_curve; (6) search completed 8/8 trials with 0 failures, test_metrics_used=false, test_locked=true. No deterministic findings are present, so no stop is warranted.

Warnings carried forward (non-blocking): (a) Model family label 'resnet18' coexists with transformer-style config fields (patch_size, num_heads, positional_encoding, pooling=cls); this naming ambiguity propagates into the abstention report provenance and OOD evidence file and could confuse downstream consumers—recommend a clarifying note in the dossier. (b) Aggregate ood_auroc (0.823189) differs from the arithmetic mean of the six per-scenario test AUROCs (0.823539) by ~0.0004, consistent with pooled-data computation, but the method is not explicitly stated in the report. (c) Validation-test accuracy gap of ~10.7 pp (0.9965 vs 0.8896) and notably weak per-class performance for cancer-associated stroma (recall 0.551) and smooth muscle (precision 0.583) mean the 2,711 human-review samples are disproportionately drawn from these classes; this should be annotated in any downstream benchmark interpretation. (d) Augmentation set (hflip, vflip, rotate180) deviates from the research-recommended set without explicit justification. None of these constitute deterministic errors in the reporting artefacts; they are documentation and performance-observation warnings that should be surfaced in the final dossier narrative.
